objective_pt: Summarise what someone said and check understanding by paraphrasing ("So what you're saying is...", "In a nutshell...", "To put it another way..."), keeping the meaning while changing the words.

teacher.goal_pt: See whether the learner can condense information and restate it in other words.
prompts: Summarise your last week in one sentence.
Summarise the plot of your favourite film in thirty seconds.
watchFor: Repeating the original words instead of paraphrasing.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat in a natural, checking tone.
exercises.prompt: So what you're saying is that we need more time.
accepted: So what you're saying is that we need more time
So what you're saying is we need more time
So what you are saying is that we need more time

exercises.explanation_pt: "Summarise" (or "sum up") = resumir. "Resume" = retomar, recomeçar. And a "résumé" (US) is a CV.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Resumindo, o projeto foi um sucesso."
accepted: In short, the project was a success
To sum up, the project was a success
In a nutshell, the project was a success
In summary, the project was a success
To summarise, the project was a success
To summarize, the project was a success
Basically, the project was a success
All in all, the project was a success

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Resume" means "retomar". For "resumindo", say "in short", "to sum up" or "in a nutshell".
commonErrors.correction_en: In short, the project was a success.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Here "success" needs the article: "was a success".
commonErrors.correction_en: In short, the project was a success.

teacher.goal_pt: Summarising and paraphrasing language: in a nutshell, the gist, to boil down to, in other words, to put it another way.
prompts: What's the gist of the last article you read?
Can you put that another way?
watchFor: "In other words" followed by the exact same words.

exercises.example_en: I didn't catch every word, but I got the gist.
In a nutshell, we need to cut costs.
To put it another way, we can't afford to wait.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.pt: o principal, o que importa no fim

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Não entendi tudo, mas peguei a ideia geral."
accepted: I didn't understand everything, but I got the gist
I didn't catch everything, but I got the gist
I didn't understand all of it, but I got the general idea
I didn't get everything, but I got the gist
I didn't understand everything, but I got the general idea
I didn't follow everything, but I got the gist of it
I didn't catch it all, but I got the gist

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Pegar a ideia" is "get the gist" or "get the general idea". "Catch" works for words you hear ("I didn't catch that").
commonErrors.correction_en: I didn't understand everything, but I got the gist.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: After "didn't", use the base form: "didn't understand".
commonErrors.correction_en: I didn't understand everything, but I got the gist.

teacher.goal_pt: Signpost summaries with a pause and a slight slowing down; pronounce "gist" and "nutshell" correctly.
prompts: Say "In a nutshell..." and pause before the point.
watchFor: Speeding up during the summary, which is the part people most need to hear.

accepted: That's the gist of it
That is the gist of it

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat. Pause after "nutshell", then slow down for the main point.
exercises.prompt: In a nutshell, the bottom line is that we need to act now.
accepted: In a nutshell, the bottom line is that we need to act now
In a nutshell, the bottom line is we need to act now

exercises.instruction_pt: Which word starts with the same sound as "gist"?
exercises.explanation_pt: "Gist" starts with /dʒ/, like "just" and "gym". "Give" and "guest" have a hard /g/.

teacher.goal_pt: Listen to a longer turn, extract the gist and paraphrase it back.
prompts: What's the main point, in one sentence?
Now say it in completely different words.
watchFor: Including every detail instead of the main idea.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. Which is the best summary?
exercises.listen: We've had three suppliers let us down this year, prices keep going up, and our own team could do the job in half the time. Honestly, I think it's time we brought production back in-house.
options: The speaker wants to find a cheaper supplier.
The speaker thinks the company should produce things itself.
The speaker wants to hire more people for the team.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Bring production back in-house" means the company should make the products itself instead of using suppliers.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and paraphrase to check you understood. Start with "So...".
exercises.listen: I'd love to help, but I've got three deadlines this week and I'm completely swamped.
accepted: So you're too busy to help this week
So you're too busy right now
So you can't help this week because you're too busy
So you don't have time this week
So what you're saying is you're too busy this week
So you're overloaded this week
So you've got too much on this week
So you're snowed under this week
So you can't help right now

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "too busy to help": "too + adjective + to + verb".
commonErrors.correction_en: So you're too busy to help this week.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The negative needs "do": "you don't have time".
commonErrors.correction_en: So you don't have time this week.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and sum up the speaker's point in one short sentence.
exercises.listen: The new app is faster, it's cheaper to run, and customers actually prefer it. I really can't see any reason to keep the old one.
accepted: So the new app is better in every way
In short, we should switch to the new app
Basically, the new app is better, so let's drop the old one
In a nutshell, the new app is better
So we should get rid of the old app
The bottom line is that the new app is better
So you think we should replace the old app
In short, the new one is better on every front

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Better" is already comparative: never "more better".
commonErrors.correction_en: In short, the new app is better in every way.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Resumindo" is "in short" or "to sum up"; "resume" means "retomar".
commonErrors.correction_en: In short, we should switch to the new app.

teacher.goal_pt: Practise active listening: the teacher talks for a minute, the learner summarises and checks understanding.
prompts: (Teacher describes a problem at length.) Can you sum that up?
Did I get that right? Paraphrase it back to me.
What would you say is the key takeaway?
watchFor: Adding opinions when asked only to summarise.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Deixa eu ver se entendi direito."
accepted: Let me see if I've got this right
Let me see if I got this right
Let me see if I understood correctly
Let me check I've understood correctly
Let me make sure I've got this right
Let me see if I've understood this properly
Just to make sure I've got this right
Let me check if I got it right

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Deixa eu ver" is "Let me see". "Leave me" means "me deixe em paz" or "vá embora".
commonErrors.correction_en: Let me see if I've got this right.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Understandable, but "if I've got this right" or "if I understood correctly" sounds more natural.
commonErrors.correction_en: Let me see if I've got this right.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Em outras palavras, precisamos cortar custos."
accepted: In other words, we need to cut costs
In other words, we have to cut costs
To put it another way, we need to cut costs
In other words, we need to reduce costs
Put simply, we need to cut costs
In other words, we've got to cut costs
In other words, we need to cut back on costs

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In general statements, say "cut costs" without "the".
commonErrors.correction_en: In other words, we need to cut costs.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Precisar" is "need". "Precise" means "preciso, exato" (adjective).
commonErrors.correction_en: In other words, we need to cut costs.

exercises.instruction_pt: Role-play: paraphrase what the client says to check your understanding.
exercises.scene_pt: A client explains what she needs for a new website.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Basically, we like the design, but the budget is tight and we need it live before the summer.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Paraphrase: so what she's saying is the design works, but cost and timing are the issues.
accepted: So what you're saying is the design works, but cost and timing are the issues
So what you're saying is that the design works, but cost and timing are the issues
So, the design works, but cost and timing are the issues
So what you're saying is the design is fine, but cost and timing are the issues
In other words, the design works, but cost and timing are the problem
So the design works, but the budget and the timing are the issues
If I understand correctly, the design works, but cost and timing are the issues

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In a statement, keep subject + verb order: "what you're saying is...".
commonErrors.correction_en: So what you're saying is the design works.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say it should be, if you simplify a couple of features.
accepted: It should be, if we simplify a couple of features
It should be doable if we simplify a couple of features
It should be, as long as we simplify a couple of features
It should be, provided we simplify a couple of features
I think so, if we simplify a couple of features
It should be possible if we simplify a couple of features

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A couple of" takes a plural noun: "a couple of features".
commonErrors.correction_en: If we simplify a couple of features.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Great. Could you put that in writing for me?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say of course, you'll send her a short summary by email today.
accepted: Of course. I'll send you a short summary by email today
Of course, I'll email you a short summary today
Sure. I'll send you a brief summary by email today
Of course. I'll send a short summary over by email today
Absolutely. I'll email you a quick summary today
Of course. I'll send you a summary by email later today

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Say "by email", without "the".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll send you a short summary by email today.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen to the colleague's message and summarise it back, checking your understanding.
exercises.prompt_en: So, the client loved the design, but they're worried about the budget, and they want to launch two weeks earlier than planned. They also asked if we could add a Spanish version later this year. Can you sum that up for the team?
guidelines_pt: Open with a summary phrase: "In a nutshell..." or "To sum up...".
Cover the main points in your own words, not word for word.
Check understanding: "Have I got that right?"

teacher.goal_pt: Final review of the C1 course themes through summarising: the learner sums up what they've learned.
prompts: Sum up the most useful thing you learned in this level.
Paraphrase this: "It's not my cup of tea."
watchFor: Copying the original instead of paraphrasing.

exercises.instruction_pt: Paraphrase this in different words: "The meeting was cancelled at the last minute."
accepted: They called off the meeting at the last minute
The meeting was called off at the last minute
They cancelled the meeting at the very last moment
The meeting got cancelled just before it started
The meeting was cancelled just before it was supposed to start
They called the meeting off at the last minute
The meeting was called off at the eleventh hour

commonErrors.match: ^the meeting was cancelled at the last minute$
commonErrors.explanation_pt: That's the original sentence. Paraphrasing means changing the words: try "called off" or "just before it started".
commonErrors.correction_en: The meeting was called off at the last minute.

exercises.sentence: I didn't catch every word, but I got the ___.
accepted: gist
idea
point

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Resume" is a false friend. Use "gist" (the main idea).
commonErrors.correction_en: I didn't catch every word, but I got the gist.

exercises.explanation_pt: "To put it another way" (or "in other words") restates an idea. "On the other hand" introduces a contrast.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat to finish the C1 course.
exercises.prompt: In a nutshell, I can now say what I mean, and mean what I say.
accepted: In a nutshell, I can now say what I mean, and mean what I say

practice.example_en: To sum up, the trial was a success.
Could you rephrase the question, please?

practice.word_en: to get the wrong end of the stick
practice.example_en: I think you got the wrong end of the stick. I never said that.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: If I've understood correctly, the deadline has moved to May.
accepted: If I've understood correctly, the deadline has moved to May
If I understood correctly, the deadline has moved to May
If I've understood correctly, the deadline's moved to May

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
accepted: Let me rephrase that
Let me just rephrase that

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: In short, we need a clearer plan.
accepted: In short, we need a clearer plan
In short, we need a much clearer plan

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with a rising, checking tone at the end.
practice.prompt: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you'd prefer to wait.
accepted: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you'd prefer to wait
Correct me if I'm wrong, but you would prefer to wait

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: Sorry, I think I got the wrong end of the stick.
accepted: Sorry, I think I got the wrong end of the stick
Sorry, I think I've got the wrong end of the stick

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Se eu entendi bem, você quer adiar o projeto."
accepted: If I understood correctly, you want to postpone the project
If I've understood correctly, you want to postpone the project
If I understand correctly, you want to postpone the project
If I understood you correctly, you want to put off the project
If I've got this right, you want to postpone the project
So if I understand you, you want to postpone the project
If I understood correctly, you'd like to postpone the project
If I understood right, you want to delay the project

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Entender bem" here is "understand correctly" or "get it right".
commonErrors.correction_en: If I understood correctly, you want to postpone the project.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Em suma, foi uma perda de tempo."
accepted: In short, it was a waste of time
In a nutshell, it was a waste of time
In brief, it was a waste of time
To sum up, it was a waste of time
Basically, it was a waste of time
Long story short, it was a waste of time
All in all, it was a waste of time
In short, it was a complete waste of time

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Perda de tempo" is "a waste of time".
commonErrors.correction_en: In short, it was a waste of time.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Resumindo a história: conseguimos o contrato."
accepted: To cut a long story short, we got the contract
Long story short, we got the contract
To cut a long story short, we won the contract
Long story short, we won the contract
In short, we got the contract
To make a long story short, we got the contract
Long story short, we landed the contract

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Resume" means "retomar". "Resumindo" is "in short" or "to cut a long story short".
commonErrors.correction_en: Long story short, we got the contract.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "A mensagem principal é que precisamos ouvir mais os clientes."
accepted: The key message is that we need to listen to our customers more
The main message is that we need to listen to our customers more
The key takeaway is that we need to listen to customers more
The main point is that we need to listen to our customers more
The bottom line is that we need to listen to our customers more
The key message is that we need to listen more to our customers
The main message is that we need to listen more to customers
The key message is that we need to listen to our clients more

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ouvir alguém" is "listen to someone".
commonErrors.correction_en: We need to listen to our customers more.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ou seja, não temos orçamento."
accepted: In other words, we don't have a budget
In other words, we don't have the budget
In other words, we have no budget
In other words, there's no budget
That is to say, we don't have a budget
So basically, we don't have a budget
In other words, we've got no budget
In other words, there's no money

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ou seja" is "in other words" or "that is to say".
commonErrors.correction_en: In other words, we don't have a budget.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and summarise it in one sentence, starting with "So basically".
practice.listen: The new system is faster and cheaper, but staff will need two weeks of training before we can switch over.
accepted: So basically, it's better but needs training first
So basically, the new system is better, but staff need training first
So basically, it's faster and cheaper, but we need two weeks of training first
So basically, it's an improvement, but it needs two weeks of training
So basically, we can switch once staff are trained
So basically, it's worth it, but training comes first
So basically, it's faster and cheaper, but staff need training first

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Training" is uncountable: "two weeks of training".
commonErrors.correction_en: Two weeks of training.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and check your understanding by paraphrasing.
practice.listen: We've decided not to renew the contract, mainly because of the delays last year.
accepted: So you're not renewing it because of the delays
So what you're saying is the delays were the main reason
So the delays are why you're not renewing
In other words, the delays cost us the contract
If I understand correctly, it's mainly because of the delays
So you're ending the contract because of last year's delays
So, in a nutshell, the delays were the deciding factor
So the main reason is the delays last year

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Before a noun, use "because of": "because of the delays".
commonErrors.correction_en: So it's because of the delays.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and give a one-sentence summary: the launch is delayed until June.
practice.listen: Could you sum up the meeting for those who missed it?
accepted: In short, the launch has been delayed until June
Basically, the launch has been pushed back to June
To sum up, the launch is delayed until June
In a nutshell, the launch is delayed until June
The main point is that the launch has been delayed until June
Long story short, the launch is now in June
The bottom line is that the launch has been put back to June
In short, the launch has been postponed until June

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A new date takes "until" or "to": "delayed until June".
commonErrors.correction_en: The launch has been delayed until June.

practice.instruction_pt: Summarise something in about a minute.
practice.prompt_en: Summarise the plot of a film or series you watched recently, then give your opinion in one sentence.
guidelines_pt: Keep only the main events: who, what and why.
Skip the details: "Without giving too much away, ..."
End with "In a nutshell, ..." and your opinion.

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play: summarise a meeting for a colleague who missed it.
practice.scene_pt: A colleague missed the morning meeting and asks you what happened.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Hey, I missed the meeting this morning. What did I miss?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say in a nutshell, the budget has been cut by ten percent.
accepted: In a nutshell, the budget has been cut by ten percent
In a nutshell, the budget's been cut by ten percent
In a nutshell, they've cut the budget by ten percent
In short, the budget has been cut by ten percent
Basically, the budget has been cut by ten percent
In a nutshell, the budget was cut by ten percent
In a nutshell, they cut the budget by ten per cent

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A change of amount takes "by": "cut by ten percent".
commonErrors.correction_en: The budget has been cut by ten percent.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Ouch. So what does that mean for our team?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say, to put it another way, you'll have to drop one of the projects.
accepted: To put it another way, we'll have to drop one of the projects
To put it another way, we're going to have to drop one of the projects
In other words, we'll have to drop one of the projects
To put it another way, we'll need to drop one of the projects
Put another way, we'll have to drop one of the projects
To put it another way, one of the projects will have to go

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The phrase is "to put it another way".
commonErrors.correction_en: To put it another way, we'll have to drop one of the projects.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say not yet; the gist was that they'll decide by Friday.
accepted: Not yet. The gist was that they'll decide by Friday
Not yet, but the gist was that they'll decide by Friday
Not yet. The gist of it was that they'll decide by Friday
Not yet. Basically, they'll decide by Friday
Not yet. The gist was they'll decide by Friday
Not yet. As far as I understood, they'll decide by Friday

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For a deadline ("até sexta"), use "by Friday".
commonErrors.correction_en: They'll decide by Friday.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Okay. So, to sum up: budget cut, one project goes, decision by Friday?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say that's it in a nutshell.
accepted: That's it in a nutshell
Yes, that's it in a nutshell
Exactly, that's it in a nutshell
That's about the size of it
Yep, that's the gist of it
That's it exactly
You've got it

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The idiom is "in a nutshell".
commonErrors.correction_en: That's it in a nutshell.

practice.instruction_pt: Which phrase checks that you have understood someone?
practice.explanation_pt: "So what you're saying is..." paraphrases the other person to check understanding.

practice.instruction_pt: What does "to get the wrong end of the stick" mean?
practice.explanation_pt: If you get the wrong end of the stick, you misunderstand what someone means.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. Which is the best summary?
practice.listen: We had a great time, honestly, but between the flights, the hotel and eating out every night, it cost us an absolute fortune.
options: The trip was fun but very expensive.
The trip was cheap and boring.
practice.explanation_pt: The speaker enjoyed the trip ("had a great time") but complains about the cost.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: So, ___ other words, the project is on hold.
accepted: in

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The phrase is "in other words".
commonErrors.correction_en: In other words, the project is on hold.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: Let me ___ that: we're not cancelling, just delaying.
accepted: rephrase
clarify

commonErrors.explanation_pt: To say it another way is "rephrase". "Resume" means "retomar".
commonErrors.correction_en: Let me rephrase that.

practice.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to check your understanding.
accepted: Correct me if I'm wrong but the budget is fixed
